info.description: CRUD API for records stored in PostgreSQL.
info.title: Records CRUD API

post.description: Checks the email and password; a wrong password and an unknown email both return 401 "invalid email or password". On success, sets an HttpOnly "session" cookie (SameSite=Strict) that the browser sends on later requests, and returns the user. Accounts can only sign in with the method they were created with (403 for google/github accounts). After 5 failed attempts per email and IP, 429 for 15 minutes.
post.summary: Sign in with an email and password

post.description: Ends the current session and clears the cookie. Requires a session.

Needs no session. Creates the organisation (name unique, ignoring case) with its four built-in roles (owner, admin, member, guest) and its first user from admin_name, admin_email and admin_password (8 to 72 bytes), who gets the owner role, in one step: the email must not be registered yet (409), and nothing is created if any part fails. Personal email providers (gmail, yahoo, ...) are rejected. The owner signs in with POST /auth/login using the email and password.

Requires a session and the user:assign_group permission (admins). The user is added to your own organisation with the member role (or the role_ids you give, which needs role:assign and permissions you hold yourself) and no group; there is no way to join an organisation without an admin. Returns the created user. A password is required (8 to 72 bytes); the user signs in with POST /auth/login using the email and password. Personal email providers (gmail, yahoo, ...) are rejected.

get.description: Returns only the groups in the given organisation (an empty list if it has none).
get.summary: List the groups of an organisation

post.description: Needs group:create. Returns the new group, including its ID. Names are lower-cased, must start with a letter, and are unique within the organisation. role_ids (IDs from GET /roles) give the group its roles and need role:assign; without them the group has none, and its members only get what their own roles allow.
post.summary: Create a group in an organisation

put.description: Sets the group's organisation and name (both required). The name must be unique within the organisation. A group that has users cannot be moved to another organisation (409).

delete.description: Fails with 409 while the group still has users; move them with the assign-group endpoint first.

get.description: Needs group:read. Every member of the group gets what these roles allow, on top of their own roles.
get.summary: List the roles of a group

put.description: Needs role:assign. Replaces the group's roles with the given role IDs (404 for a role that does not exist in the organisation). You can only add or remove roles whose permissions you hold yourself (403 otherwise). Takes effect for the members on their next request.
put.summary: Change the roles of a group

get.description: Returns the name and email of every user in the group (an empty list if the group has no users).
get.summary: List the users in a group

get.description: The organisation of the signed-in user; no id is needed. 404 for a user without an organisation. Requires a session.

put.description: Admins only (403 for members). The new name must be unique, ignoring case. Requires a session.

delete.description: Admins only (403 for members). PERMANENTLY deletes the organisation, its groups, all its users (the caller included) and all their records, in one transaction. confirm_name must be the organisation's exact name (400 otherwise). The users' sessions stop working immediately. Requires a session.

get.description: Needs role:read. Returns the permissions a role can be given, with a description and the resource they belong to.

With user_id: that user's records (record:read:own for yourself, record:read:org for others). With scope=org: every record of your organisation (needs record:read:org). With neither: your own records. An empty list if there are none.

parameters.description: Use org for every record of your organisation
parameters.name: scope

post.description: The record belongs to the user given by user_id (404 if the user doesn't exist).
post.summary: Create a record for a user

get.description: Needs role:read. Includes the four built-in roles (owner, admin, member, guest).
get.summary: List the roles of your organisation

post.description: Needs role:create. Creates a role in your own organisation. permissions (keys from GET /permissions) are what the role allows; you can only give permissions you hold yourself (403 otherwise, 400 for an unknown key). Names are lower-cased, must start with a letter, and are unique within the organisation (409).

put.description: Needs role:update. The built-in roles cannot be renamed (400).

delete.description: Needs role:delete. Fails with 409 while a user or group still has the role, and the built-in roles cannot be deleted (400).

get.description: Needs role:read. Returns the permission keys of the role.

put.description: Needs role:update. Replaces the role's permissions with the given keys from GET /permissions (400 for an unknown key). You can only add or remove permissions you hold yourself (403 otherwise), and the built-in roles cannot be changed (400). Takes effect for everyone who has the role on their next request.

get.description: Needs user:read. Returns every user of your own organisation, oldest first, including those without a group.
get.summary: List the users of your organisation

put.description: Changes the name only: the email is the login identity and cannot be changed (an email field is rejected). Needs user:update:own for yourself, user:update:org for others. The group is changed with the assign-group endpoint and the roles with the roles endpoint.

delete.description: Fails with 409 while the user still has records; delete those first.

put.description: Needs user:assign_group. The group must exist (404) and belong to the organisation stored on the user (400 otherwise). A group_id of 0 takes the user out of their group. The user gets the roles of the new group and loses those of the old one, so you must hold the permissions of every role that changes (403 otherwise).
put.summary: Assign a group to a user

get.description: Needs role:read, except for yourself. Returns every permission the user has: the union of their own roles and the roles of their group.
get.summary: List what a user may do

get.description: Needs role:read, except for yourself. These are the roles given to the user themselves; the roles their group gives are listed under GET /groups/{id}/roles.
get.summary: List the roles a user holds directly

put.description: Needs role:assign. Replaces the roles the user holds directly with the given role IDs (404 for a role that does not exist in the organisation). You can only add or remove roles whose permissions you hold yourself (403 otherwise), so only an owner can give or take the owner role, and an organisation always keeps at least one owner (409). Takes effect on the user's next request.
put.summary: Change the roles of a user

organisation_id.description:
OrganisationID is the owner's organisation, stored with the record so
organisation-wide permissions can be checked without loading the owner.
It is 0 (omitted) for records of legacy users without an organisation.

group_id.description:
GroupID is the user's group, which always belongs to OrganisationID (the
database enforces it with a composite foreign key). A user without an
organisation has both as 0 (NULL in the database, omitted from JSON).

signup_method.description: SignupMethod is how the user was created (SignupMethod* constants).

role_ids.description:
RoleIDs are IDs from GET /roles. Leave the field out for a group with no
roles.

admin_password.description: AdminPassword is the owner's password (8 to 72 bytes).

permissions.description:
Permissions are keys from GET /permissions. Leave the field out for a
role with none.

role_ids.description:
RoleIDs are IDs from GET /roles. Leave the field out to give the user the
member role.
